nodes.label: DSL-driven vs hand-written split
nodes.community_name: CV Pipeline and Legacy Theme Page
nodes.rationale: The DSL drives content, translations, section order (sectionOrder, sidebarOrder), palette, display overrides (hideOnHtml / hideOnPdf) and off-schema extras (dailyLife, work.projects); layouts, CSS, interactive JavaScript, XSLT logic and favicon geometry stay hand-written.

nodes.label: Single-sheet PDF hard constraint + fit loop
nodes.community_name: CV Pipeline and Legacy Theme Page
nodes.norm_label: single-sheet pdf hard constraint + fit loop
nodes.rationale: Every PDF must fit on one sheet (recto/verso, two pages maximum); a fit loop walks through progressively tighter plans and fails hard rather than shipping a three-page CV.

nodes.label: CV pipeline (single source to 6 languages, 3 web views, 6 PDFs)
nodes.norm_label: cv pipeline (single source to 6 languages, 3 web views, 6 pdfs)
nodes.rationale: One custom DSL source fans out to every output so content, translations, ordering and branding never diverge between the site, the XML/XSLT themes and the PDFs.

nodes.label: Deterministic byte-identical pipeline
nodes.rationale: Recompiling the same source yields the same output down to the byte.

nodes.label: No paths filter on workflow triggers
nodes.norm_label: no paths filter on workflow triggers
nodes.rationale: Tests read scripts/ and the README's marker structure; a paths filter narrower than that dependency set is how a workflow quietly stops firing. The suite takes a second, so running it on every push and pull request costs nothing.
